question: The foreign exchange reserve of India dropped to levels that were ______ during 1991 economic crisis.

options.text: not sufficient for even fifteen days

solution:
The correct answer is __**not sufficient for even fifteen days**__**.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **foreign exchange reserve of India** in 1991 dropped to a critical level, which was **not sufficient for even a fifteen-day**** **worth of imports.
 
• This crisis was a result of **high fiscal deficits**, **rising oil prices** due to the Gulf War, and a significant **balance of payments deficit**.
 
• India's reserves had depleted to a mere **$1.2 billion**, which was inadequate to cover its essential imports, creating an economic emergency.
 
• To tackle this crisis, the Indian government had to approach the **International Monetary Fund (IMF)** for a bailout and pledged its gold reserves as collateral.
 
• This economic crisis eventually led to the introduction of the **1991 Economic Reforms**, including **liberalization, privatization, and globalization (LPG reforms)**, which significantly transformed the Indian economy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Causes of the 1991 Economic Crisis:**

 
 
• **High fiscal deficit:** The government's expenditure far exceeded its revenues, leading to unsustainable fiscal imbalances.
 
• **Oil price shock:** The Gulf War in 1990-91 caused a sharp rise in global oil prices, putting additional pressure on India's import bill.
 
• **Balance of Payments (BoP) crisis:** India faced a severe BoP crisis due to a sharp decline in foreign exchange reserves.
 
• **Mounting external debt:** India's external debt was unsustainable, and servicing this debt became increasingly challenging.
 
 
 
• **Measures Taken to Resolve the Crisis:**
 
 
• **Pledging gold reserves:** India pledged **67 tonnes of gold** to the Bank of England and other financial institutions to secure loans.
 
• **IMF bailout:** India sought a loan from the IMF under its **Structural Adjustment Program** to stabilize the economy.
 
• **Economic reforms:** The government initiated a series of reforms under the leadership of **Dr. Manmohan Singh**, then Finance Minister, to liberalize the economy.
 
 
 
• **1991 Economic Reforms:**
 
 
• **Liberalization:** Removal of licensing requirements and restrictions on industries to promote private sector participation.
 
• **Privatization:** Disinvestment of public sector enterprises to improve efficiency and reduce the fiscal burden.
 
• **Globalization:** Opening up the Indian economy to foreign investment and international trade.
 
 
 
• **Impact of the Reforms:**
 
 
• **Economic growth:** Post-1991, India's GDP growth accelerated, and the country emerged as one of the fastest-growing economies.
 
• **Increased foreign investment:** The liberalization of the economy attracted significant foreign direct investment (FDI).
 
• **Export growth:** Indian industries became more competitive globally, leading to an increase in exports.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Foreign Exchange Reserves:** These are assets held by a central bank in foreign currencies, used to back liabilities and influence monetary policy.
 
• **Balance of Payments (BoP):** It is a statement that summarizes a country's economic transactions with the rest of the world over a specific period.
 
• **Structural Adjustment Program:** A set of economic policies imposed by the IMF or World Bank as a condition for financial assistance to stabilize and reform the economy.
 
• **Fiscal Deficit:** It represents the gap between the government's total expenditure and its total revenue, excluding borrowings.
